blocks.orig: Mikumi National Park is one of the southern national park in Tanzania. Its open horizons and abundant wildlife draws frequent comparisons to the more famous Serengeti Plains. The park borders the Selous Game Reserve to the south and the two areas form a unique ecosystem. The chance that you will encounter lions climbing trees here is greater than in other parks!
blocks.html: Mikumi National Park is one of the southern national parks in Tanzania. Thanks to its wide horizons and plentiful wildlife, it is often compared to the better-known Serengeti Plains. To the south it borders the Selous Game Reserve, and together the two areas form a single, unusual ecosystem. Here your odds of spotting lions up in the trees are higher than in other parks!

blocks.orig: The park has a great variety of animals and most visitors come to this National Park aiming to spot four of the ‘Big Five’ – leopard, lion, elephant and buffalo. It’s a great place for a Tanzania vacation, you will enjoy it! Hippos live in a pair of mud pools and are one of the highlights. These are situated 5 km north of the main entrance gate. They are supported by an ever-changing cast of water-birds.
blocks.html: A wide range of animals live in the park, and most visitors arrive at this National Park hoping to see four of the ‘Big Five’: leopard, lion, elephant and buffalo. It makes a wonderful destination for a Tanzania vacation, and you are sure to enjoy it! One of the highlights is the hippos, which live in a pair of mud pools 5 km north of the main entrance gate, accompanied by an ever-changing cast of water-birds.

blocks.orig: The Mkata Foodplain is a wide area in Mikumi National Park that is very good for wildlife viewing. Lions survey their grassy kingdom – and the zebra, wildebeest, impala and buffalo herds that migrate across it – from the flattened tops of termite mounds, or sometimes during the rains, from perches high in the trees. Giraffes forage in the isolated acacia stands that fringe the Mkata River, islets of shade favoured also by Mikumi’s elephants. Mkata Foodplain is perhaps the most reliable place in Tanzania for sightings of the powerful eland, the world’s largest antelope. The equally impressive greater kudu and sable antelope haunt the miombo-covered foothills of the mountains that rise from Mikumi National Park’s borders.
blocks.html: Within Mikumi National Park, the broad Mkata Foodplain is an excellent area for watching wildlife. From the flattened tops of termite mounds, or in the rainy season sometimes from perches high in the trees, lions keep watch over their grassy realm and the herds of zebra, wildebeest, impala and buffalo that migrate across it. Giraffes browse in the scattered acacia stands along the Mkata River, pockets of shade that Mikumi’s elephants also favour. The Mkata Foodplain is possibly the most dependable spot in Tanzania to see the powerful eland, the largest antelope on earth. The no less impressive greater kudu and sable antelope roam the miombo-covered foothills of the mountains rising along the borders of Mikumi National Park.

blocks.orig: Mikumi is a good place for bird lovers as it is also home to more than 400 different species of birds!
blocks.html: With more than 400 different bird species recorded, Mikumi is also a fine destination for bird lovers!

blocks.orig: The Mkata River offers majestic views of fishing Open-billed Storks. Marabou stork, Red-billed oxpeckers, Black-bellied bustard, Francolin, Cattle egret, Guinea-fowls, Hornbill and Malachite Kingfischer are common birds in Mikumi National Park. The most colourful species are the Yellow-throated long claw, the Lilac-breasted roller and the Bateleur eagle. European migrants are common in Mikumi National Park during the rainy season.
blocks.html: Along the Mkata River you can enjoy majestic views of Open-billed Storks fishing. Birds commonly seen in Mikumi National Park include the Marabou stork, Red-billed oxpeckers, Black-bellied bustard, Francolin, Cattle egret, Guinea-fowls, Hornbill and Malachite Kingfischer. The most colourful of all are the Yellow-throated long claw, the Lilac-breasted roller and the Bateleur eagle. In the rainy season, European migrants are frequently spotted in Mikumi National Park.

blocks.html: Expert travel tips for Mikumi National Park

blocks.orig: My name is Aaron and I am a guide at Mikumi National Park for 10 years. In Mikumi you can spot the four of the Big Five, although they are a bit harder to find than in the northern parks. Most of our guests are impressed with the hippos and birds.
blocks.html: I am Aaron, and I have guided in Mikumi National Park for 10 years. Four of the Big Five can be seen in Mikumi, though they take a little more effort to find than in the northern parks. The hippos and the birdlife leave the strongest impression on most of our guests.

blocks.orig: Some tips on when and how you can best be /get there:
blocks.html: A few tips on the best time to go and how to get there:

blocks.orig: Avoid the wet months, I do advice to go from June until October, because the park is not accessible during wet months (March to May).
blocks.html: Stay away in the wet months; my advice is to visit between June and October, since the park cannot be reached during the wet season (March to May).

blocks.orig: Put this park in the beginning of your trip, so that the trip builds up on the right way, Selous and Ruaha are definitely the highlights.
blocks.html: Schedule this park at the start of your trip, so the journey builds up in the right order: Selous and Ruaha are without doubt the highlights.

blocks.orig: Don’t combine Mikumi with Selous by car. The driving distance is way too far (whole day and not very comfortable roads), this should be done by plane.
blocks.html: Do not combine Mikumi with Selous by road. The drive is far too long (a full day on fairly uncomfortable roads); take a plane for this leg instead.

blocks.orig: Mikumi National Park is one of the southern national parks in Tanzania and borders Selous Game Reserve. Its abundant wildlife draws frequent comparisons to the famous Serengeti. The chance that you will encounter lions climbing trees here is greater than in other parks!
blocks.html: Mikumi National Park, one of Tanzania’s southern national parks, shares a border with Selous Game Reserve. Its rich wildlife often earns comparisons with the famous Serengeti. Your odds of seeing lions up in the trees are better here than in other parks!

blocks.orig: Since the completion of the paved road connecting the park gate with Dar es Salaam, Mikumi National Park has become easily accessible for safaris and it takes a six to seven hours drive from Dar Es Salaam.
blocks.html: Now that the paved road between Dar es Salaam and the park gate is complete, Mikumi National Park is easy to reach for safaris: the drive from Dar Es Salaam takes six to seven hours.

blocks.orig: Mikumi National Park borders the Udzungwa National Park and Ruaha National Park.  The three locations make a varied and pleasant safari circuit.
blocks.html: Mikumi National Park shares borders with Udzungwa National Park and Ruaha National Park. Together, the three destinations make up a varied and enjoyable safari circuit.
